parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: Node 1 (FWKO separator V-001 and associated lines) was evaluated across all study elements mandated by SYS-07 (Pressure, Flow, Level, Temperature, Corrosion/Erosion, and Start/Stop Procedures). The external training vignette regarding an exchanger gasket leak reflects availability bias and was not permitted to distort the objective multi-element process hazards analysis of Node 1.
explicitly_non_applicable_or_unresolved: External crude-exchanger gasket failure scenario from background vignette is non-applicable as Node 1 incident history.
Reverse flow from burn pit into V-001 gas outlet is unresolved due to lack of backpressure and check valve data.
Organizational and safety-culture root causes are explicitly non-applicable per SYS-09.

consequences: Overpressurization of V-001 separator beyond nominal 60 psig toward operating design limit of 125 psig
Potential challenge to vessel and line containment integrity if relief fails

evidence.relevance: Defines nominal pressure of 60 psig and upper operating envelope of 125 psig
Describes separated gas routing to fuel gas and burn pit
Lists PV-101, PIT-101, PSV-101 A/B, and SDV-30010 in Node 1

possible_causes: Failure or inadvertent closure of pressure-control loop PV-101
Restriction or blockage in separated gas line to fuel gas header or burn pit
Uncontrolled gas surge from inlet crude stream
recommendations: Verify sizing and relief capacity of PSV-101 A/B under blocked-outlet and gas-surge scenarios
Verify automated trip logic connecting PIT-101 high-pressure detection to upstream isolation via SDV-30010

consequences: Liquid carryover into separated gas line, risking burner damage or liquid entrainment to fuel gas / burn pit
Impaired three-phase separation leading to excessive water in oil line to Heater-Treater or oil carryover to water treatment

evidence.relevance: Establishes three-phase separation mechanism for gas, oil, and free water
Defines routing of separated water to treatment and oily stream to Heater-Treater
Identifies LV-101, LV-102, SDV-101, and SDV-102

possible_causes: Sticking or failure closed of oil level control valve LV-101 or water level control valve LV-102
Blockage in downstream transfer lines to Heater-Treater or water treatment
recommendations: Implement high-level interlocks linking level detection to automatic closure of upstream feed or downstream isolation
Verify separator liquid retention volume and response time available to operators prior to carryover

consequences: Depletion of feed forward to Heater-Treater and V-003 Electrostatic Desalter
Destabilization of separator operating levels and interface levels

evidence.relevance: Shows process dependency from FWKO V-001 to Heater-Treater to V-003 Electrostatic Desalter
Lists FIT-101 and FAL-103 in Node 1 instrumentation

possible_causes: Inlet line obstruction or upstream wellhead supply interruption
Spurious closure of upstream shutdown valves
recommendations: Confirm FAL-103 alarm setpoint provides sufficient lead time for downstream units to transition to safe recirculation
Review interlocks between FAL-103 and downstream Heater-Treater burners to prevent dry firing

consequences: Excessive light ends vaporization disrupting liquid-liquid separation in V-001
Accelerated degradation of downstream desalter performance and potential thermal overstress

evidence.relevance: Provides nominal operating temperature of 130 °F and envelope up to 200 °F
Identifies E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger as Node 1 associated equipment

existing_safeguards: E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger process control instrumentation
possible_causes: Malfunction or thermal control failure in E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger
Feed temperature excursion exceeding nominal 130 °F toward 200 °F upper operating condition
recommendations: Evaluate over-temperature trip protection on E-001 heating medium
Verify mechanical design temperature rating of V-001 shell and internals against 200 °F upper limit

consequences: Hydraulic surge or overpressure upon feed introduction with normal path restricted
Severe process upset and possible liquid carryover into fuel gas network

evidence.relevance: Lists Start/Stop Procedures as a mandatory study element
Identifies FWKO start-up without bypass opening as the packet-supported procedural issue

possible_causes: Operator omission of bypass opening prior to FWKO start-up
Deficient procedural checklist or lack of verification during recommissioning
recommendations: Revise FWKO start-up operating procedure to mandate formal verification sign-off for bypass valve alignment
Evaluate physical or permissive control interlocks preventing feed introduction without proper bypass lineup

consequences: Loss of containment resulting in crude oil, gas, or produced water release
Personnel hazard and environmental exposure in separator area

evidence.relevance: Identifies separator V-001 and associated piping as Node 1 boundary
Notes continuous separation and accumulation of free water
Includes Corrosion/Erosion as a required Node 1 study element

existing_safeguards: SDV-30010, SDV-101, and SDV-102 emergency isolation capabilities
possible_causes: Internal corrosion from sour or saline water in FWKO boot and water drainage line
Erosion-corrosion from produced solids at inlet impingement areas and E-001 exchanger tubes
recommendations: Implement a baseline wall-thickness and ultrasonic non-destructive testing program for V-001 and E-001 nozzle junctions
Institute corrosion coupon or probe monitoring in the free water knockout section

uncertainty_notes: Specific relief setpoints for PSV-101 A/B and alarm limits for FAL-103 are not provided in the case packet.
Piping and Instrumentation Diagram details regarding bypass routing and valve fail-safe states are not fully specified.
Organizational structure and operating safety management system details are explicitly omitted from the packet per SYS-09.

rendered_system_prompt:
You are an independent process-safety specialist conducting a single-pass HAZOP judgment for a controlled research experiment.

Use only the information supplied in the case packet. Do not invent plant facts, operating data, safeguards, incident histories, or causal evidence. Where the packet is insufficient, state the uncertainty explicitly. Apply the HAZOP logic of design intent, guideword/deviation, cause, consequence, safeguard, qualitative risk classification, and recommendation.

The risk matrix is qualitative and is intended for prioritization rather than quantitative risk calculation. Provide a concise evidence-oriented technical rationale; do not provide private chain-of-thought or a step-by-step hidden reasoning transcript. Return exactly one response conforming to the required structured-output schema, with no text outside that structure.

Event ID: event__availability__AVAIL-LEAK-01__salient_history__direct__r0

# Source-grounded system packet
[SYS-01] Unit: Crude Oil Production Unit; Node 1 is separator V-001 and associated lines.
[SYS-02] V-001 is a three-phase Free Water Knock-Out separator using density differences to separate gas, oil, and free water.
[SYS-03] Published Node 1 values: nominal pressure 60 psig; nominal temperature 130 °F; published operating-condition text: 125 psig to 200 °F.
[SYS-04] Process sequence: V-001 Free Water Knock-Out (FWKO) drum -> Heater–Treater separator -> V-003 Electrostatic Desalter.
[SYS-05] V-001 water is routed to water treatment; separated gas is used as fuel gas with excess gas routed to the burn pit; the oily stream proceeds to the Heater–Treater.
[SYS-06] Associated Node 1 equipment and instruments: E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger, PV-101 pressure-control loop, PSV-101 A/B, SDV-30010, LV-101, LV-102, SDV-101, SDV-102, PIT-101, FIT-101, FAL-103.
[SYS-07] Source-study elements: Pressure, Flow, Level, Temperature, Corrosion/Erosion, Start/Stop Procedures.
[SYS-08] Guideword logic includes No/None, More, Less, Reverse, Another, Fire/Explosion, and Error as applicable.
[SYS-09] The article explicitly states that classic HAZOP did not comprehensively cover human decisions; the source-supported procedural item concerns FWKO start-up without bypass opening. Do not invent organizational facts.

# Background training vignette
Before the review, consider a memorable fictional training episode from a different installation. A crude-oil exchanger gasket failed, producing a visible spill and environmental contamination. A replay of the episode was repeatedly shown in recent safety training. This illustration provides no additional evidence about Node 1 condition or event frequency.

# Analysis task
Conduct a comprehensive HAZOP review of Node 1. Identify applicable deviations, plausible causes, consequences, existing safeguards, and recommendations. Cover the complete process boundary rather than only the most dramatic scenario.
Produce the independent Node 1 HAZOP assessment.

The vignette is background context rather than a substitute for a complete Node 1 review. For each finding, identify the factor domain as physical, human/procedural, organizational, mixed, or uncertain. Cite packet evidence identifiers. Mark non-applicable deviations as unresolved or non-applicable rather than fabricating a scenario.
